_comment: Services whose container health signal cannot go red for a real outage.
scripts/check_health_claims.py enforces the shape: an entry with no reason, no owner,
or a past expiry is itself a failure, because a stale waiver is another claim nobody
2026-07-26: EMPTY. Both waivers were discharged the day they were written, neither by
kernel       - the healthcheck now probes /readyz. The deferral rested on a coupling
measurement showed is not real (stopping the fleet-worker does not
flip it; the stack-tool receipt is cached in Redis). Forcing the
schema head to 0037 on dev made the container unhealthy while
/healthz kept answering 200 - the 2026-07-25 client outage reproduced
fleet-worker - the probe is now `boltrig fleet-health`, which reads back the signed,
short-lived tool receipt the worker itself publishes and the kernel's
/readyz already consumed. The waiver said there was no readiness
endpoint to point at, which was true and beside the point: the
readiness EVIDENCE existed, and nothing on the worker side read it.
An empty file is not a dead file. The gate still runs, and a new first-party service
whose healthcheck cannot see an outage lands here or turns the build red.
